ASIA 100.title: Introduction to Traditional Asia
ASIA 100.description: A survey of the histories and cultures of Asia before 1600 and the coming of the Europeans. Emphasis will be given to parallel themes in the development of the civilizations of South, Southeast and East Asia.

ASIA 101.title: Introduction to Modern Asia
ASIA 101.description: A survey of the emergence of modern Asia. Aims at an understanding of how the various peoples of Asia have maintained distinctive cultural identities despite centuries of political, economic, social and cultural change.

ASIA 110.title: Introduction to Religions in Asia
ASIA 110.description: A survey of religious traditions of Asia, including communities, professionals, practices and beliefs of small-scale and large-scale societies. Approaches and theories drawn from the field of religious studies.

ASIA 150.title: Asian Internets
ASIA 150.description: The cultures of contemporary Asia through an exploration of the uses, form, and content of online media from and about Asia.

ASIA 200.title: Cultural Foundations of East Asia
ASIA 200.description: A comparative survey of the beliefs, assumptions and values which have shaped the civilizations of East Asia in both traditional and modern times.

ASIA 208.title: Cultural Foundations of South Asia
ASIA 208.description: A survey of South Asian cultures, including language and literature, art, religion, polity and society, as they developed in the past and have been transformed in the modern period.

ASIA 209.title: Cultural Foundations of Southeast Asia
ASIA 209.description: A comparative survey of the different cultures found in the communities of Southeast Asia. Focus will be on language and literature, arts, religion, society and polity, ideologies and belief systems in the past as well as in modern times.

ASIA 210.title: Traditions of Yoga
ASIA 210.description: Philosophical, religious, and cultural development of yoga in classical and medieval South Asia and its relation to contemporary globalized practice.

ASIA 211.title: Sex, Sexual Ethics, and Asian Religions
ASIA 211.description: Sex and sexual ethics in the scriptures, monastic rules, rituals, and narratives of Asian religions, such as Sikhism, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Confucianism.

ASIA 212.title: Writing About Japan
ASIA 212.description: Literary, historiographic, religious, and feminist approaches to Japanese myths, legal tracts, religious tales, fiction, and poetry.

ASIA 213.title: Myth, Literature, and Film in North India
ASIA 213.description: Indian literary and mythological texts, in genres from epic to lyric, as recast in contemporary Hindi film.

ASIA 222.title: Encountering Asia
ASIA 222.description: Introduction to the literary, religious, and philosophical traditions of at least two Asian cultures using foundational texts. Students will learn about these traditions by encountering them historically as well as through the lenses of their own diverse identities and contexts.

ASIA 223.title: Writing Asia
ASIA 223.description: This writing-intensive course is to be taken concurrently with ASIA 222. The seminar builds on the materials of ASIA 222. Students must have knowledge of or be enrolled in the study of one of the languages offered in Asian Studies.

ASIA 250.title: Introduction to Buddhism
ASIA 250.description: Origins, basic teachings, development of Theravada, Mahayana, and Tantric traditions, historical spread first through Asia and later the world, and Buddhism in contemporary societies.

ASIA 254.title: Sex, Gender, and Sexuality in Japanese Literature and Film
ASIA 254.description: The integral role that sex, gender, and sexuality play in literary and cinematic works from Japan. Literary works will be read in translation, movies will be subtitled.

ASIA 258.title: Religion in South Asia
ASIA 258.description: The major religious traditions of South Asia, including Hinduism, Islam, Sikhism, and Buddhism; the significance of religious thought and practice in premodern India, as well as the continuing impact of religion in today's globalized South Asia.

ASIA 270.title: China in World History
ASIA 270.description: The history of China in a global context, from the earliest times to the most recent past; how China has changed the world and how engagement with the world has changed China.

ASIA 300.title: Writing and Culture in East Asia
ASIA 300.description: Practical, aesthetic, historical, technological and political issues pertaining to the use of Chinese characters - hanzi (Chinese), kanji (Japanese), or hanccha (Korean) - throughout the region.

ASIA 301.title: Buddhism in the Modern Era
ASIA 301.description: Buddhism from the nineteenth century to present day with special emphasis on its history and character in local settings, including specific traditions such as Tibetan Nyingma and Japanese Zen, as well as the development of a modern and global Buddhism.

ASIA 302.title: Theravada Buddhism
ASIA 302.description: History, story, and culture of the major form of Buddhism primarily focused on the regions of Sri Lanka, and mainland Southeast Asia, including southern Vietnam, parts of southern China, spread to Nepal, and modern global diffusion.

ASIA 303.title: Mahayana Buddhism
ASIA 303.description: Historical and philosophical development of Mahayana Buddhism.

ASIA 304.title: Survey of South and Southeast Asian Performing Arts
ASIA 304.description: An historical perspective of the performing arts of South and Southeast Asia, highlighting the role of music, dance, and the dramatic arts in the lives of actors and audiences. Option to complete a practicum performance.

ASIA 305.title: Asian Horror Cinema: National Nightmares and Specters of Trauma
ASIA 305.description: Engaging with the ideologies, industrial histories, socio-cultural contexts, and aesthetics of horror films - and the genre itself - from various Asian cinemas.

ASIA 306.title: Esoteric Buddhism
ASIA 306.description: Overview of Buddhism's rich and complex esoteric traditions in the Himalayan region and South, Southeast, and East Asia, with particular emphasis on texts, commentaries, and practices from a variety of traditions, locales and time periods.

ASIA 307.title: Korean Language and Writing in Culture and Society
ASIA 307.description: An examination of Korean language and writing using approaches from sociolinguistics, the sociology of language, and linguistic anthropology.

ASIA 308.title: Myth, Ritual and Epic in Ancient India
ASIA 308.description: Myths of creation Gods and goddesses of the Vedic pantheon. Connections with myths in other parts of the world, particularly in the Indo-European tradition. Literary representations of the myths.

ASIA 309.title: South Asian Beyond South Asia
ASIA 309.description: A history of South Asian peoples and communities that emigrated overseas, including Indo-Canadians.

ASIA 310.title: Studies in the History of a Major Asian Civilization
ASIA 310.description: Study of an Asian culture area different from those covered in existing courses. Not given every year. Consult Department for details. May be taken multiple times on different subjects for credit.

ASIA 311.title: Tibetan Buddhism
ASIA 311.description: Religious terrain of the Tibetan cultural realm, looking at the history and development of Tibetan Buddhism and key ideas of the four main Tibetan Buddhist traditions.

ASIA 312.title: Buddhism in Korea
ASIA 312.description: Historical, cultural and philosophical development of Korean Buddhism.

ASIA 313.title: Tibetan and Himalayan Culture and Society
ASIA 313.description: History and culture of the Himalayan regions, including India, China, Tibet, Nepal, and Bhutan.

ASIA 314.title: Premodern Japan
ASIA 314.description: Japanese history (political, economic, social and cultural) to 1600.

ASIA 315.title: Japan from Feudal to Modern State
ASIA 315.description: Japanese history from 1600 to the Meiji Restoration. Political, economic, social and cultural forces which were involved in transforming Japan.

ASIA 316.title: Race and Ethnicity in Japanese Literature and Film
ASIA 316.description: Examines relations between majority and minority groups in Japanese society and changing definitions of Japan through literature and film from Japan.

ASIA 317.title: The Rise of Korean Civilization
ASIA 317.description: The evolution of a distinctive Korean civilization within the East Asian cultural sphere. Primary focus on cultural, social and political development from the earliest times to the sixteenth century.

ASIA 318.title: Premodern India
ASIA 318.description: A survey of the history and culture of India from the earliest historic period to 1200 and the coming of Islam, with emphasis on the evolution of classical Hindu civilization.

ASIA 319.title: Contemporary Chinese Popular Cultures
ASIA 319.description: Chinese popular cultures of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries, in relation to social changes, national policies, individual choices, everyday experience, and globalization.

ASIA 320.title: History of Early China
ASIA 320.description: History of China from the earliest times to the disintegration of the Tang empire. Students will acquire the analytical skills and tools to understand the origins and foundations of Chinese society.

ASIA 321.title: Celebrity Culture in Chinese Societies
ASIA 321.description: Histories, controversies, and implications of celebrity culture in Chinese societies, with a focus on the entanglement of author, audience, and media across different sociopolitical contexts.

ASIA 323.title: History of Cantonese Worlds
ASIA 323.description: The history, culture, languages, and identities of the multi-faceted Cantonese worlds, in the context of Chinese history and the Cantonese diaspora.

ASIA 324.title: Literature of Hong Kong
ASIA 324.description: A survey of the literature of Hong Kong, from classical times to the present. Important periods in literary history (imperial, colonial, post-colonial), major authors (locals, visitors, and writers elsewhere), and important genres, including poetry, essays, and fiction.

ASIA 325.title: Hong Kong Cinema
ASIA 325.description: A survey of the cinema of Hong Kong from the post-war period to the present. The influence of Hong Kong on global cinema, and the forces (artists, studios, audiences, etc.) that have given rise to filmmaking styles and genres perceived as distinctively Hong Kong.

ASIA 326.title: Critical Approaches to Manga and Anime
ASIA 326.description: A critical introduction to Japanese manga and anime in the 20th and 21st centuries.

ASIA 327.title: Korean Popular Music in Context
ASIA 327.description: History, contexts, and the genres of Korean popular music. Students will analyze specific artists and songs using a range of approaches. While an understanding of basic concepts of music will be helpful, no previous exposure to ethnomusicology or music performance is required.

ASIA 328.title: Modern Islam
ASIA 328.description: History, culture, values, and sociopolitical movements of the Islamic world from 1500 to the modern day; interconnections between power, politics, gender, and the arts in modern Islamic societies. Recommended as a basis for all other Islamic studies courses.

ASIA 329.title: Gender in South and Southeast Asia
ASIA 329.description: A critical examination of what it means to be a woman or a man within the social and cultural context of South and Southeast Asia. What masculinity and femininity signify in these societies; how these concepts are reaffirmed or challenged.

ASIA 330.title: Muslims in Modern South Asia
ASIA 330.description: The history of Muslims in modern South Asia from colonialism to the present.

ASIA 331.title: Islam in South Asia (750-1750)
ASIA 331.description: The history of Islam in South Asia beginning with the first Indo-Islamic interactions, the crystallization of Sufi traditions and sultanates, through the rise of European colonialism.

ASIA 332.title: Confucianism in China and Beyond: Reinventions of Tradition
ASIA 332.description: Key ideas and trends in Confucian thought and practice from its origins to modern times through primary sources in translation and secondary scholarship.

ASIA 333.title: Contemporary South Asian Gender and Sexuality Studies
ASIA 333.description: Main theories and key concepts with a particular focus on the changing status of women, and gender and sexual minorities.

ASIA 334.title: Writing Women in Premodern East Asia
ASIA 334.description: The construction of gender in literary writings by and about women in select areas of premodern East Asia.

ASIA 335.title: Cantonese Music
ASIA 335.description: A history of musical genres with Cantonese lyrics from the nineteenth century to the present. Topics include music and text relationships, major singers, major genres (narrative songs, Cantonese opera, Cantopop).

ASIA 336.title: Sufi and Bhakti Devotional Literatures
ASIA 336.description: Sufi and Bhakti thought and tradition in South Asia through literary works in translation.

ASIA 337.title: The Korean People in Modern Times (1600 to the present)
ASIA 337.description: The transformation of Korea from a Confucian state into an industrial nation. The rise of nationalism and modern ideologies in Korea. Cultural, social and economic changes Korea has undergone as it has entered the modern world.

ASIA 338.title: India in the Age of Empire and Revolution
ASIA 338.description: History of India from the rise of the British East India Company to the beginnings of Indian nationalism and anti-colonial rebellion in the 19thcentury.

ASIA 339.title: The Construction of South Asian Communities in the Diaspora
ASIA 339.description: An examination of contemporary South Asian communities in the diaspora. Topics of particular importance are family life, religious life, notions of space, communal memory, literary and visual representation.

ASIA 340.title: History of Later Imperial China
ASIA 340.description: History of China from the end of Tang to the eve of its modern transformation. Students will acquire the analytical skills and tools to understand the political, socio-economic, and cultural changes in imperial China.

ASIA 341.title: Classical Chinese Literature in Translation
ASIA 341.description: Poetry, historical and philosophic prose writings and the earliest genres of fiction in classical Chinese (ca. 1100 BC ca. 750 AD).

ASIA 342.title: Chinese Literature in Translation: The Vernacular Tradition
ASIA 342.description: Readings in drama and fiction, 800 to 1800 AD. The emergence of vernacular genres as distinct from and sometimes opposed to the existing classical genres.

ASIA 343.title: Film in South Asia
ASIA 343.description: Social and cultural history of South Asian film.

ASIA 344.title: Topics in Japanese Cultural History I: Aristocrats and Warriors
ASIA 344.description: Focuses each year on a specific topic related to the courtly or warrior culture of Japan.

ASIA 345.title: Chinese Film Classics
ASIA 345.description: Introduction to and analysis of artistically significant films made in mainland China during the first half century of Chinese film history.

ASIA 346.title: Topics in Japanese Cultural History II: The Early Modern Age
ASIA 346.description: Focuses each year on a specific topic related to the culture of early modern Japan.

ASIA 347.title: Traditional Korean Literature in Translation
ASIA 347.description: An introduction to Korean literature from ancient times to 1900.

ASIA 348.title: Poetic Life in Classical India
ASIA 348.description: Cultural explorations in the poetry, theatre, and ornate prose writings of India in the classical period (c. 300-1300 CE).

ASIA 349.title: Ecoculture and Literature in Japan
ASIA 349.description: Ecocultural approach to reading, analyzing, and writing about narratives written in Japan from premodern times to the present.

ASIA 350.title: Asian Literature in Translation: A Comparative Approach
ASIA 350.description: A comparative approach to the literatures of East, South and Southeast Asia focusing on a specific theme.

ASIA 351.title: Modern Chinese Fiction in Translation
ASIA 351.description: Reading of selected novels and stories written between 1750 and the present.

ASIA 352.title: Topics in Traditional Chinese Vernacular Literature
ASIA 352.description: Traditional Chinese culture as seen through reading and discussion of exemplary literary works in the vernacular language.

ASIA 353.title: Introduction to Hindi Film
ASIA 353.description: History, aesthetics, politics, and social roles of Bollywood films. Films will be subtitled.

ASIA 354.title: Introduction to Japanese Cinema
ASIA 354.description: Students will be introduced to the work of the major directors (e.g., Ozu, Mizoguchi, Kurosawa, Itami, Oshima, Shinoda). Ideological uses of literary texts and period pieces (e.g., Ugetsu, Life of Oharu, Double Suicide). Impact of depiction of Japanese in American film.

ASIA 355.title: History of Chinese Cinema
ASIA 355.description: Introduction to the work of major directors.

ASIA 356.title: Korean Cinema
ASIA 356.description: Introduction to the work of the major film makers.

ASIA 357.title: Modern Korean Literature in Translation
ASIA 357.description: Selected fiction and poetry written between 1917 and the present.

ASIA 358.title: Literature of Medieval India in Translation
ASIA 358.description: Devotional, mystic, and erotic poetry of medieval Hinduism, Islam, and Sikhism.

ASIA 359.title: Afghan History
ASIA 359.description: Afghan history as it unfolded from the Eurasian empires to the modern era of nation-building and internationalism.

ASIA 360.title: A Specific Asian Literature in Translation
ASIA 360.description: Introduction to the literature of a linguistic area of Asia not covered in existing courses. Not given every year. Consult the Department for details. May be taken multiple times on different subjects for credit.

ASIA 361.title: Modern Chinese Fiction in Translation II
ASIA 361.description: A thematic survey of modern Chinese fiction and film in translation.

ASIA 362.title: Pre-Modern Japanese Fiction (in translation)
ASIA 362.description: The influential genre of early tales and fiction in pre-modern Japan.

ASIA 363.title: Fiction and Film from Modern Taiwan
ASIA 363.description: A reading-intensive survey of literary and cinematic culture in Taiwan since the early 20th century: colonialism, the national divide, nativism, trauma, cosmopolitanism, and utopian imaginings.

ASIA 364.title: Modern Japanese Literature in Translation
ASIA 364.description: An introduction to the literature and cultural history of modern Japan, with readings drawn from various literary genres, from 1868 to the present.

ASIA 365.title: Punjabi Cinema
ASIA 365.description: Punjabi culture, history, and social values through films. The class includes film viewings and seminar discussions. Films will be subtitled.

ASIA 366.title: Topics in Asian Studies
ASIA 366.description: Thematically-organized topics in Asian literature, history, visual culture, religion, or communities. Topics vary from section to section. Consult Department for current offerings.

ASIA 367.title: Contemporary Korean Culture
ASIA 367.description: An introduction to the literature, drama, music, and art of Korea today. Particular attention will be paid to the continuing influence of traditional themes and forms.

ASIA 368.title: Modern Literatures of South Asia in Translation
ASIA 368.description: Fiction, drama, and/or poetry of modern India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and/or Sri Lanka, including works in translation and/or originally written in English.

ASIA 369.title: Asian Folklore
ASIA 369.description: A survey of oral and expressive traditions in Asia, including jokes, superstitions, fairy tales, myths, music, and foodways; practical training in collecting and archiving folklore.

ASIA 370.title: The Sanskrit Cosmopolis: India and the World, 200-1500 CE
ASIA 370.description: Languages, religions, art forms, and political structures of Asian societies shaped by creative encounters with Sanskrit.

ASIA 371.title: Foundations of Chinese Thought
ASIA 371.description: Early (pre 221 BCE) Chinese thought (Confucianism, Daoism, Mohism, Legalism), its contemporary implications, and the role of philosophy and religion in human flourishing./

ASIA 372.title: Development of Traditional Chinese Thought
ASIA 372.description: Chinese thought from the Han dynasty (206 BCE to 220 CE) to Wang Yangming (1472-1529) in its historical and cultural contexts.

ASIA 373.title: History of Hong Kong
ASIA 373.description: History, culture, and identities of Hong Kong from the early 1800s to the present.

ASIA 374.title: Imagining Punjab
ASIA 374.description: The cultural and linguistic region of Punjab as it has been imagined in different times and places, in South Asia and beyond, in literature, scholarship, film, and popular culture.

ASIA 375.title: Global Chinese Cinemas
ASIA 375.description: A survey of Chinese cinemas in global perspective, covering films, filmmakers, producers, audiences, markets, industries, and critical discourse since the early twentieth century. Covers both cinematic culture and filmmaking technique.

ASIA 376.title: The Sikhs: Formations, Contexts, and Historical Development
ASIA 376.description: Introduction to the historical development of Sikh traditions in India and Diaspora, from the 15th century to the present, with attention to broader historical contexts.

ASIA 377.title: History of Korean Thought
ASIA 377.description: An examination of Korean religious, philosophical, and scientific thought from the earliest written records to the present day, with particular focus on the interaction of Shamanism, Buddhism, Confucianism, and, in the present century, Christianity.

ASIA 378.title: Philosophical Wisdom of Early India
ASIA 378.description: Epistemological and ontological thought from the Vedic period to the period of the rise of philosophical schools or systems Philosophy in the Mahabharata, Gita; early Buddhist and Jain views on knowledge and reality; views on language.

ASIA 379.title: The Persian Book of Kings
ASIA 379.description: The Persian Shahnameh (the Book of Kings) and its context in Iranian myth and history. Analysis of the poem through lenses of gender and sexuality, race/ethnicity, and religion.

ASIA 380.title: Modern Arabic Literature from the Middle East and North Africa in Translation
ASIA 380.description: Analysis and critique of 20th and 21st century Modern Arabic prose writing emerging from the Middle East and North Africa in translation.

ASIA 381.title: Daoist (Taoist) Religion and Its Philosophical Background
ASIA 381.description: A study of the Daoist religious traditions from their beginnings in the second century CE in their cultural, intellectual and social contexts.

ASIA 382.title: Buddhism in China
ASIA 382.description: History, thought, and practices of Chinese Buddhism from its beginnings until the twentieth century.

ASIA 383.title: Korean History Through Film
ASIA 383.description: Modern Korea's historic moments through a cultural lens. Examines how film as cultural product reflects, challenges, and distorts history. Emphasis on formations of gender, class, and national identities.

ASIA 384.title: The Zhuangzi (Chuang-Tzu)
ASIA 384.description: Introduction to a foundational text of East Asian thought. Both the primary text and its reception in traditional and modern contexts will be examined.

ASIA 385.title: Chan/Zen Buddhism: Doctrine and Practice
ASIA 385.description: The history, doctrines, and practices of Chan Buddhism, particularly the profound influence of Chan Buddhism on various aspects of East Asian culture.

ASIA 386.title: Chinese Grammar and Usage I
ASIA 386.description: Analysis of modern Chinese grammar and its usage in various discourses, situating its form and function in relation to social and cultural contexts. Recommended pre-requisites: One of CHIN 207, CHIN 337, CHIN 208, CHIN 338, CHIN 217, CHIN 347, CHIN 218, CHIN 348, or a higher level of Chinese language proficiency.

ASIA 387.title: Japanese Religions
ASIA 387.description: An introduction to traditional Japanese religions including Shinto, Buddhism, Shugendo, Confucianism, new religions and folklore, and their roles in Japanese history, culture and society.

ASIA 388.title: Classical South Asian Philosophy
ASIA 388.description: Debates on issues of epistemology, language and ontology among the philosophical traditions of classical South Asia. ASIA 378/PHIL 378 is recommended.

ASIA 389.title: Life Writings of South Asian Diasporic Women
ASIA 389.description: Auto/biographies and life writings of South Asian women in the Diaspora. Emphasizes theories of representation, subjectivity, agency, difference, and memory.

ASIA 390.title: History of the Indian Ocean World
ASIA 390.description: Societies and empires shaped by voyages of exploration, religious pilgrimages, trading diasporas and forced migration in the world of the Indian Ocean.

ASIA 391.title: Classical Islam
ASIA 391.description: History and culture, values, and achievements of Islamic societies from 700-1500; interconnections between power, politics, gender, and the arts in Islamic societies. Recommended as a basis for all other Islamic studies courses.

ASIA 392.title: Classical Persian Literature in English Translation
ASIA 392.description: Works of classical Persian literature dating from the tenth to the seventeenth century.

ASIA 393.title: History of Iran from the Sasanians to the Safavids
ASIA 393.description: Iranian history from the fall of the Sasanian empire and the Arab conquest of Iran to the rise of Iranian dynasties in the east, the reign of Turkic and Turko-Mongolian rulers, and the formation of a Shi'ite Iran under the Safavids.

ASIA 394.title: Post-Revolutionary Iranian Cinema
ASIA 394.description: Gender politics, family relationships, and women's social, economic, and political roles in post-revolutionary Iran as shown through Iranian cinema.

ASIA 395.title: Modern Persian Literature
ASIA 395.description: Modern Persian literature, including fiction, drama, and/or poetry, of Iran, Afghanistan, and/or Tajikistan dating from the mid-19th to the 21st century (in English translation).

ASIA 396.title: Chinese Grammar and Usage II
ASIA 396.description: Analysis of modern Chinese grammar and its usage in various discourses, situating its form and function in relation to social and cultural contexts. Continuation of ASIA 386. Recommended pre-requisite: ASIA 386 or higher level of Chinese language proficiency.

ASIA 397.title: The Idea of India
ASIA 397.description: History of cultural ideas that led to India's transformation from a traditional, colonial society tied to the British empire to a postcolonial, pluralistic, development oriented parliamentary democracy.

ASIA 398.title: Narrative Literature in Premodern India
ASIA 398.description: Stories of gods, goddesses and religious heroes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, Puranas, Avadanas and in classical poetry and drama.

ASIA 399.title: Films of the South Asian Diaspora
ASIA 399.description: Contemporary films of the South Asian Diaspora, with a focus on Canada, US, and UK. Emphasizes theories of representation, visual and cultural analysis.

ASIA 400.title: Chinese Characters: Script, Languages, and Civilizations
ASIA 400.description: Advanced study of the structure of the Chinese characters in their graphic, phonetic, and semantic aspects. Recommended pre-requisites: ASIA 300 and one of CHIN 207, CHIN 208, CHIN 337, CHIN 338, CHIN 217, CHIN 218, CHIN 347, CHIN 348, JAPN 213, JAPN 251, JAPN 323, JAPN 361, KORN 300, KORN 301, KORN 302.

ASIA 402.title: Language, Writing, and Linguistic Thought in the History of the Sinographic Cosmopolis
ASIA 402.description: History of language, writing and linguistic thought in China, Japan, Korea and Vietnam from a comparative perspective and focusing on the dissolution of this translocal cultural formation with the onset of modernity. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors only.
notes: Recommended: At least 12 credits of any level of CHIN_V, JAPN_V, or KORN_V or placement approval

ASIA 403.title: Language and Colonialism in East Asia
ASIA 403.description: Classic works on language and colonialism in British India and imperial Japan. Emphasis on language policies, linguistic thought, language ideology, questions of assimilation and identity, and the consequences of colonialism for Asian languages today.

ASIA 403.prerequisiteText: 4th year standing. 400-level standing (or equivalent) in Chinese, Japanese or Korean (can be concurrent)

ASIA 405.title: The Interaction of Science, Religion, and Philosophy in East Asia
ASIA 405.description: The influence of Confucianism, Buddhism, Daoism, and Christianity on the way peoples of East Asia understood and manipulated the natural world, focusing on the natural sciences.

ASIA 407.title: North Korea in Historical Context
ASIA 407.description: Analytical overview of North Korea's politics, society, and economy. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 408.title: Religion, Society, and Secularism in Modern India
ASIA 408.description: The postcolonial nation-state and the challenge of a multi-religious society. Religious and secular discourse in colonial India, the partition, the modern constitution, secularism, Hindu and Muslim mobilization, and religious radicalism and communal violence Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 410.title: International Relations in Premodern East Asia
ASIA 410.description: International relations, particularly between Korea and Japan in the premodern East Asian context, focusing on migration, trade, diplomacy, war, collective memory, mutual perceptions, and the context of the Sinocentric international order.

ASIA 411.title: Chinese Political Thought and Institutions
ASIA 411.description: Chinese theories and practices of government and administration from earliest times to 1949.

ASIA 412.title: Pre-Modern Chinese Poetry (Pre-Qin to Tang)
ASIA 412.description: Features and evolution of major pre-Chinese poetry from the 11th century B.C.E. to the 10th century C.E.; analytical reading of signature poems by selected poets in English translation in the pre-modern Chinese poetic tradition during this historical period.

ASIA 413.title: Pre-Modern Chinese Poetry (Tang to Qing)
ASIA 413.description: The features and evolution of pre-Chinese poetry from the 10th century to the 19th century; analytical reading of signature poems by selected poets in English translation in the pre-modern Chinese poetic tradition during this historical period.

ASIA 414.title: Architecture and Urbanism in Islamic South Asia
ASIA 414.description: Historical factors shaping Indian architecture from the 13th to the 19th centuries.

ASIA 418.title: Social History of India
ASIA 418.description: Fundamental institutions including family, caste and religious organizations, with emphasis on the early modern and British periods.

ASIA 419.title: Economic History of India
ASIA 419.description: Examines the material foundations of Indian history. Considers India's place in the premodern world, different phases of globalization, processes and legacies of European colonial rule, and the development of India's modern economy.

ASIA 427.title: Topics in Korean Popular Culture (Hallyu)
ASIA 427.description: A survey of one of the primary areas of Korean popular culture, such as television dramas, film, K-Pop music, graphic novels and webtoons, or Hanshik cuisine. Recommended pre-requisites: one of ASIA_V 327, ASIA_V 347, ASIA_V 357, ASIA_V 447, ASIA_V 452, ASIA_V 457, or placement approval.

ASIA 428.title: Mughal India
ASIA 428.description: History of the politics, economy, society, and culture of South Asia from the Great Mughals to the British conquest.

ASIA 429.title: Rebels, Martyrs, and Outlaws in Early Modern Japan
ASIA 429.description: The social history of early modern Japan with a particular focus on the patterns of organized protests, rebellions, and movements under samurai rule.

ASIA 430.title: International Relations in Modern East Asia: Korea and Japan
ASIA 430.description: Trade, diplomacy, war, imperialism, militarism, colonialism, collective memory, mutual perceptions Korean-Japanese relations are examined as an exemplary case for exploring the dimensions of international conflict and partnership.

ASIA 431.title: Tibetan Literature, Genres, and Book Culture
ASIA 431.description: Tibetan literature, textual genres, and book and printing culture from the seventh century to the present.

ASIA 433.title: Representations of Muslims in Hindi/Urdu Films
ASIA 433.description: Depictions of Muslims in relation to the majoritarian community as well as other minorities in South Asian cinema, with a particular focus on the Hindi/Urdu film industry.

ASIA 436.title: The Partition of India in Film and Narrative
ASIA 436.description: Analysis and critique of how the partition of India is depicted in fictional literary works and feature films.

ASIA 440.title: Cultural History of Imperial China
ASIA 440.description: An in-depth examination of the construction, transmission, and transformation of Chinese culture(s) prior to 1800. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 441.title: Masterworks of Chinese Fiction and Drama in Translation
ASIA 441.description: Reading of a classic novel or play, with attention to intellectual, social, and political subtexts as well as aesthetic dimensions and problems of interpretation.

ASIA 442.title: Lives of Chinese Books
ASIA 442.description: Concepts and methods for understanding the lives of books across time, through an examination of both the material forms of a text and its cultural reception. Focus on one major work from pre-modern China. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 443.title: National Narratives in Chinese Literature and Film
ASIA 443.description: Nationhood as it is constructed, deconstructed, and continuously contested in Chinese literature, film, and other media from the late imperial period to the 21st century in mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and the Chinese diaspora. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies.

ASIA 444.title: Topics in Modern Japanese Fiction and Cultural History
ASIA 444.description: Focuses on a limited time period or particular aspect of modern Japanese literature.

ASIA 445.title: Japanese Crime Fiction
ASIA 445.description: Examines representations of crime and criminality in modern and contemporary Japanese literature. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 447.title: Korean Women's Literature
ASIA 447.description: Women's voices and issues in the Korean literary tradition, from earliest times to the new millennium, in translation. Recommended pre-requisites: one of ASIA 347, ASIA 357. Permission of instructor is also acceptable.

ASIA 448.title: Narrative and Performance in South Asia
ASIA 448.description: Key theoretical issues in the production and enactment of folk narratives in traditional and modern South Asian cultures. Intended for advanced undergraduates in Asian folklore studies. Recommended pre-requisite: ASIA 369.

ASIA 450.title: Special Topics in Buddhist Studies
ASIA 450.description: For upcoming offerings, including course descriptions, please see section information in the UBC course schedule at

ASIA 451.title: Modern Chinese Authors in Translation
ASIA 451.description: Study of one influential modern Chinese author, such as Lu Xun, Shen Congwen, Eileen Chang, Yu Hua, Mo Yan, or Wang Anyi. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 452.title: Literature of the Korean Diaspora
ASIA 452.description: A survey of literature, in translation, from the Korean diaspora, focusing on writing by ethnic Koreans in North America, Europe, and Japan. Recommended pre-requisites: one of ASIA 347, ASIA 357, ASIA 447, ASIA 457.

ASIA 453.title: Japanese Travel Literature
ASIA 453.description: Japanese travel literature (myths, legends, poetry, tales, diaries, illustrated guides, satiric sermons, haiku, comic fiction, colonial reporting, and ethnography) from the 8th century to present. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 454.title: Japanese Poetry in Translation
ASIA 454.description: An introduction to Japanese poetry from its origins in song and myth, to its development from a courtly art (waka) to a popular pastime (haiku). Influences on prose, autobiography, and theatre will also be considered.

ASIA 455.title: Adaptations of Japanese Classics
ASIA 455.description: Introduction to literary, stage, and film adaptations of Japanese classics and legends and the ways in which these new works appropriate the past to comment on the present.

ASIA 456.title: History and Culture of Taiwan
ASIA 456.description: The major social, economic, political, and cultural changes in Taiwan since the seventeenth century; the post-World War II process of democratization and Taiwan's place in the contemporary world.

ASIA 457.title: The Modern Korean Novel
ASIA 457.description: Survey of major single-volume novels, ranging from Yi Kwang-su's Heartlessness to Ch'oe Yun's There a Petal Silently Falls, in translation. Recommended pre-requisite: ASIA 357, or permission of instructor.

ASIA 458.title: Gender and Sexuality in Classical Persian Literature
ASIA 458.description: Premodern Persian texts (in translation) and construction of femininities, masculinities, and sexuality. Restricted to students with third-year standing or above.

ASIA 459.title: Gender, Sexuality, and Feminism in Sikhi (the Sikh Religion)
ASIA 459.description: Gender, sexuality, and feminism in the Sikh religious tradition, surveying early modern, colonial, and post-colonial readings through Sikh religious text, ritual, and life. This course is recommended for students who have some knowledge of Sikh Studies, religious studies, and/or gender and sexuality studies. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

ASIA 460.title: Modern Asian Women in Narrative
ASIA 460.description: Experience of women in the context of a particular Asian culture, as seen through literature, popular culture, film and folklore. Narrative as a medium for the representation and constitution of gender.

ASIA 461.title: Gender and Sexuality in Modern Iranian Narratives
ASIA 461.description: Literary, cinematic, folk, and/or popular culture texts from modern Iran. Emphasis on constructions and contestations of masculinities and femininities, as they intersect with sexuality, race, ethnicity, ability, and/or religion.

ASIA 462.title: Japanese Cinema and Genre
ASIA 462.description: An exploration of Japanese cinema and the relationship between film genre theories discursive constructed conventions and sociocultural norms, as well as how artists challenge those norms.
notes: A minimum of 6 credits of 300-level ASIA coursework, particularly ASIA 354, recommended.

ASIA 463.title: Japanese Documentary Media
ASIA 463.description: Historical survey of Japanese documentary film and media, including press, photography, reality TV shows, and social media.

prerequisite.raw: Restricted to students with 2nd year standing or above

ASIA 463.prerequisiteText: Restricted to students with 2nd year standing or above

ASIA 464.title: Japanese Women's Self-Writing
ASIA 464.description: Selected aspects of the more than 1000 years of self-writing (diary, autobiography, personal fiction). Theory and criticism about the use of writing as a medium of self-expression.

ASIA 465.title: Japanese Horror
ASIA 465.description: The genre of Japanese visual horror explored through formal visual literacy, genre theory, and textual analysis.

ASIA 466.title: The History of Christianity in Asia
ASIA 466.description: A survey of Christian proselytizing drives in South, Southeast, and East Asia, focusing on the period since 1500 and the reasons for successes (the Philippines and Korea, for example) and failures (Japan).

ASIA 468.title: Approaches to the Study of Asian Religions
ASIA 468.description: The Western genealogy and problematics of religion, issues in its application to non-Western cultures and traditions, and the practical study of Asian religions, in Asia and its diasporas. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors. Recommended pre-requisites: one of ASIA_V 376, ASIA_V 381, ASIA_V 382, ASIA_V 383, ASIA_V 387.

ASIA 470.title: Comparative Conceptions of the Self
ASIA 470.description: Ways in which the self has been portrayed in eastern and western religious traditions. Thinkers to be considered include Aristotle, Mencius, Freud, Xunzi (Hsn-tzu), Nietzsche, and Zhuangzi (Chuang-tzu).

ASIA 474.title: From the Chronicle to the Archive: Cultures of History in South Asia
ASIA 474.description: Examines how South Asian pasts have been memorialized in writing, from medieval chronicles to the development of history as a modern academic discipline in the nineteenth century.

ASIA 475.title: Documenting Punjabi Canada
ASIA 475.description: Exploration of the history of the Punjabi Canadian community through traditional text-based methods and oral history collection.

ASIA 476.title: Topics in South Asian Studies
ASIA 476.description: Seminar class designed to explore current scholarly debates in South Asian and Sikh Studies. May be repeated for credit with permission of instructor.

prerequisite.raw: Restricted to students with 2nd year standing or above

ASIA 476.prerequisiteText: Restricted to students with 2nd year standing or above

ASIA 477.title: New Religious Movements of East Asia
ASIA 477.description: Examines the rise of new religious movements in China, Japan, and Korea over the last two centuries, from the Taiping, Tonghak, and Tenri-kyo to the Unification Church, SGI International, and Falun Gong. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 478.title: The Religious Image in Asia
ASIA 478.description: The religious image and related material culture within Buddhism, Islam, Jainism, Hinduism, Christianity, and Sikhism with special attention to methodological concerns.

prerequisite.raw: Restricted to students with 2nd year standing or above

ASIA 478.prerequisiteText: Restricted to students with 2nd year standing or above

ASIA 484.title: The History of the Choson Dynasty
ASIA 484.description: Political, social, and cultural history of Korea's Choson Dynasty, focusing on how it lasted from 1392 to 1910 and why it collapsed so quickly at the beginning of the twentieth century.

ASIA 485.title: Inventing Asian Religions in the West/East Encounter
ASIA 485.description: An examination of how western imperial expansion transformed the descriptions and practices of Asian traditions through systems of classification, missionaries, discovery of languages, modernity, and fragmentation.

ASIA 488.title: Religion, Society and State in Modern India
ASIA 488.description: History of secular and religious discourse in post-independent India. Partition, state policy of secularism, religious mobilization among Hindus and Muslims, communal violence and religious radicalism.

ASIA 490.title: Asian Classics - Fourth Year Seminar
ASIA 490.description: Focus changes from year to year. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 491.title: India and the Persianate World
ASIA 491.description: Histories of Muslim Empires, spanning Iran, India and Central Asia, from 1000-1800 CE. Examined through the conceptual lens of the Persianate World with emphasis on Persianate culture and power in South Asia. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 495.title: Folk Cultures in the Asian Diaspora
ASIA 495.description: The mediation of folklore (e.g. slang, songs, games, dance, foodways) in the everyday lives of immigrant and transnational Asian communities. Emphasis on Asian-Canadian folklore in Greater Vancouver through digital documentary media production and archival folklore research. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 498.title: Asia in Museums and Beyond
ASIA 498.description: Museological representations of Asia and Asian forms of museological representation in colonial and post-colonial contexts. Restricted to fourth-year Asian Studies majors.

ASIA 499.title: Honours Thesis
ASIA 499.description: Restricted to fourth-year students admitted to the Honours Program in Asian Studies.

ASIA 502.title: Modern Chinese Fiction in Global Perspective
ASIA 502.description: Modern Chinese literature in relation to concepts such as world literature, the Sinophone, nationalism, cosmopolitanism, globalization, and critical theory.

ASIA 511.description: Selected readings from primary texts in Confucianism, Taoism and Buddhism, and popular religion.

ASIA 516.title: Race and Ethnicity in Asian Studies

ASIA 517.title: Chinese Media Studies: Theories and Histories

ASIA 518.title: New Media and Asia
ASIA 518.description: New media theory, technologies, industries, cultures, and analytical practices with a focus on transnational Asian interactive media such as video games, mobile apps, social media, video streaming sites and services, and online fan networks.

ASIA 519.title: Popular Cultures in Asia
ASIA 519.description: Critical engagement with different disciplinary approaches to the study of Asian popular cultures.

ASIA 524.title: Japanese for Specialists of China and Korea
ASIA 524.description: Reading seminar in Japanese scholarly material dealing with China and/or Korea for graduate students who have a reading knowledge of Chinese and/or Korean and some knowledge of Japanese.

ASIA 590.description: Focus changes from year to year, please check the Department website for current course syllabi.

ASIA 591.title: Critical Issues in Asian Studies
ASIA 591.description: Proseminar introducing major methodological and conceptual themes in the contemporary study of Asia, modern and pre-modern. Required of all Asian Studies Ph.D. students, normally in their first year.

ASIA 592.title: The Profession of Asian Studies
ASIA 592.description: Introduction to essential skills for academic and professional work in Asian Studies. Outlines career trajectories in the Ph.D. and beyond, including grant applications, cv-writing, and job searches. Required of Asian Studies Ph.D. students, normally in their first year.

ASIA 699.title: Doctoral Dissertation
ASIA 699.description: In Chinese, Japanese, Korean, or South Asian Studies only.
